doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: Learning from James Brown's rhythm
summary: Rowe and LaLama agree on what horns and rhythm sections behind James Brown teach; Rowe then asks which big band leader he enjoyed most.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You know I think you can learn a lot, even if you’re a jazz player, from listening to what those horn players are playing behind him and all those things.

Yeah. And the rhythm section, the feeling. The feeling. James Brown — I still love it. I mean to me that’s how good it is. When I put it on now, after all I’ve been through in a musical sense, I still enjoy it as much. So to me that’s true art. That might not be in the books as art, but to me it is. Because I get a kick out of it. It’s not just nostalgic either. It’s a feeling.
You had your big band experiences under three kind of different leaders. You had Mel Lewis and Buddy Rich and Woody Herman. Who did you enjoy the most?
